title: Minimum Cost to Buy Apples
summary: Given n cities and a 2D array of roads with associated costs, along with an array indicating the cost to buy an apple in each city, determine the minimum total cost to buy an apple from each city.
statement: Given n cities and a 2D array of roads with associated costs, along with an array indicating the cost to buy an apple in each city, determine the minimum total cost to buy an apple from each city. This total cost includes the cost of traveling to any city to buy an apple and then returning to the starting city, with the cost of all roads multiplied by a given factor k.
constraints: Cities are numbered 1 through n and roads are undirected weighted edges.
Starting from each city, buy one apple in any city and include round-trip travel priced at (k+1) times the one-way shortest distance.
Return the minimum total cost for every starting city.
hints: Run Dijkstra from each starting city.
For every settled city, combine its apple price with shortest distance times k+1 and keep the minimum.
Dijkstra supplies exact nonnegative shortest paths, and evaluating every purchase city gives the exact best total for each start.
editorial: Dijkstra supplies exact nonnegative shortest paths, and evaluating every purchase city gives the exact best total for each start.

tests.explanation: Comparing local purchases with shortest-path travel gives costs [54,42,48,51].
City 1 can travel to city 2 and buy for total 1+2*3=7, while city 2 buys locally for one.
